findings.reason: the section that orders the releases permits a split that the release bar makes permanently uncuttable.
findings.text: s3's done-when refuses every group "when a family of the group has a member in another group", but s2's done-when merely lists the families whose members sit in more than one group and explicitly puts "any proposed split or merge of a group" to the lead as an allowed choice, and neither s2 nor s3 nor s5 states how a cross-group family is cleared (a joint cut of both groups, a member move, or a lead-ruled exception); families share a stem across physics domains by construction, so a group whose family straddles two of them is refused by its own bar and no node's verdict can close it

findings.reason: without a control name of known answer the census cannot fail, and the release order and group rates derived from it carry that undetected error into every later section.
findings.text: s2's done-when requires per-group live counts, the count whose domain is among its sources' domains, and the audit's wrong-domain count, with no planted member whose answer is known, so a source-domain join or domain read that silently matches nothing produces a uniform census (every count zero or every count "agrees") that reads as success and then fixes the ranking that s4 and s5 are ordered by
